title: Varkala and Wayanad (Batch 7)
selection: Batch 7. Varkala and Wayanad each had 4 sections. Adds who it's for, best time, practical info, food, safety (Wayanad), FAQs and mistakes, with fuller overviews as pending suggestions. Wayanad now notes the 30 July 2024 landslides and monsoon risk. No prices.

overview.text:
Varkala, about 50 km north of Thiruvananthapuram, is the one place on Kerala's flat coast where sea cliffs rise above the beach — a National Geological Monument. Below them is Papanasam beach, named for a spring believed to wash away sins.

The 2,000-year-old Janardhana Swamy Temple, the 'Varanasi of the South', stands above the beach, and Sivagiri Mutt holds the samadhi of Sree Narayana Guru. There are jet skis, parasailing and surf lessons at Kappil, quiet Thiruvambadi beach under the northern cliffs, and day trips to Anjengo Fort, the Varkala tunnel and Ponnumthuruthu island. It stays calmer than Kovalam. Come October to March; it has its own railway station.

overview.text:
Wayanad — from Vayal Nadu, 'land of paddy fields' — is Kerala's highland district on the borders of Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, part of the UNESCO-recognised Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve. Robusta coffee grows here under forest shade between 700 and 2,100 m, and the hills hold Chembra peak with its heart-shaped lake, the Edakkal rock shelter with carvings as old as 6000 BC, Banasura Sagar, India's largest earthen dam, and the Muthanga and Tholpetty wildlife ranges.

Wayanad has no railway: Kozhikode station is 90–110 km away and Calicut airport 65–93 km, up the Thamarassery ghat road. October to May is best. The monsoon brings landslide risk — in July 2024 landslides near Meppadi were among the deadliest in Kerala's history — so check local alerts before travelling in the rains.
